answer: A reputation stake that decays works like this: every agent must lock a deposit that vests slowly, so a newcomer cannot instantly buy influence. A zephyr of fresh identities may register for free, but without staked history they can only read, not vote or claim rewards. As an agent does useful verified work, its weight grows, and a gale of fake accounts would each need real locked capital and months of honest behavior to matter. Misbehavior slashes the stake, making a haven for honest agents: attacking costs more than the rewards it could steal, so sybils stay unprofitable.
